title: Access handoff dry-run, synthetic backfill, and customer safeguards playbook
creator: Ava Chen
description: Playbook for executing a safe migration from RBAC v1 to RBAC v2 focused on data integrity, audit forwarding, SSO/SAML mapping verification, and admin control guardrails. Includes a dry-run plan using synthetic tenants, a resumable backfill with checksum and drift detectors, idempotent dual-write mode, staged cutover waves, rollback signals, and customer communication templates.
primary_goals: Guarantee no permission regressions for existing customers
Preserve and forward audit trails to SIEM without gaps
Validate SAML/SSO role mappings during migration dry-runs
Provide fast, observable rollback with minimal service disruption
Minimize on-call handoffs by automating sanity gates and telemetry
success_criteria: Parity: dual-read parity >= 99.99% in canary wave for 48h
Backfill integrity: checksum + row-count reconciliation pass for all waves
No production-security incidents attributable to migration
Audit continuity: no more than 1 minute of audit-forwarding lag during cutover
Customer opt-in/visibility: Customer dashboard shows migration status and a one-click rollback for enterprise seats
assumptions: Dedicated telemetry pipelines (kinesis -> datalake) can accept 2x current audit volume
Dual-write path is backwards compatible for v1 read traffic
We can create synthetic tenants that mimic P95 workspace complexity
SAML identity attributes map deterministically to RBAC v2 schema for >95% customers
plan_summary: 1) Run dry-run on staging with synthetic tenants and real traffic replay. 2) Enable idempotent dual-write in prod for low-risk customers. 3) Run resumable backfill with chunked workers and checksum reconciliation. 4) Open canary wave with 5% of orgs, observe parity and audit metrics for 48h. 5) Expand waves 25%->100% with automated gating and customer notice. 6) Final cutover toggles v1-read->v2-read and disable dual-write after verification. 7) Post-cutover monitoring and 7-day audit review.
detailed_steps: Dry-run/staging: deploy migration branch with --dry-run flag, replay 7 days of production traffic from replay bucket (s3://replay/rbac/2026-02). Verify SAML mapping scripts against recorded assertions.
Synthetic tenants: provision 20 synthetic workspaces that span small/medium/large org shapes, with seeded role graphs and policy edge-cases (nested teams, inheritance, external groups).

Dual-write: enable dual-write service with idempotency keys and dedupe layer. All writes routed to both v1 and v2 stores. Dual-read parity mode to sample reads from both stores and emit parity events to telemetry.

Backfill: resumable job that processes workspaces in priority waves (internal, trial, small customers, mid-market, enterprise). Each chunk computes a SHA256 checksum of role blobs and emits pre/post counts. Failed chunks are retried with exponential backoff and alert to #rbac-migration-alerts.

Parity checks: continuous parity asserts comparing effective permission checks for random actor-resource-action triples. Parity failures auto-create numbered incidents and surface to on-call with repro payloads.
Audit forwarding: ensure audit events contain v2 metadata and are forwarded to SIEM with sequence numbers. Implement a short-lived buffering store to prevent loss during transient outages.
SSO/SAML verification: run mapping reconciliation tool that compares SAML attributes in identity provider logs vs. RBAC v2 role assignments. Flag >5% mismatch orgs for manual review.
Gated rollout: waves with gates: metric gates (parity, error budget, backend latency), security gates (no new high-severity findings), and business gates (customer opt-outs accounted).

Cutover: run Cutover Orchestrator job to switch read path from v1 to v2 for eligible orgs. Maintain traffic shadowing for 24h and keep v1 in read-only mode for 7d for reconciliation or emergency rollback.
Rollback: immediate toggle to v1-read fallback using traffic-proxy toggle. Documented rollback runbook with steps to re-enable v1-read, trigger re-sync, and notify customers.
Post-mortem & audit: after full cutover, run a 7-day audit comparison and publish findings to execs and affected customers. Update docs and SDKs as needed.
gating_metrics: On-call page volume from migration (target < 2 pages/day during waves)
SAML mapping mismatch ratio (target < 2% for non-enterprise orgs)
API latency delta for auth checks (target < +15ms p95)
rollback_triggers: Parity drop below 99.9% for a sustained 30m window
Significant customer-reported permission regressions (>=3 independent reports in 1 hour)
Unrecoverable backfill corruption detected by checksum mismatches >0.01% of objects
implementation_notes: Dual-write ensures write durability while allowing safe reads from v1 during early waves. Make dual-write idempotent by using client-provided operation_id and last-applied timestamps.
Backfill jobs must be resumable and observe consistent snapshot semantics. Use optimistic concurrency control for large role graphs.
Telemetry must include deterministic parity keys so we can deduplicate and trace mismatches to raw payloads.
Audit-forwarding uses sequence numbers to detect gaps; sequence store is replicated and has a 24h TTL for retries.
Add an admin UI flag 'migration_hold' tied to org metadata that prevents cutover for orgs with open compliance requirements.
risks: Complex SAML mappings for enterprise customers could require manual mapping adjustments and delay waves
Unexpected policy semantics in RBAC v2 causing subtle permission regressions
Audit pipeline capacity issues under peak load causing temporary lag
Backfill corruption risk if snapshot is not stable across chunked workers
Human error during manual cutover steps if automation is incomplete
mitigations: Pre-identify top-50 enterprise customers and run one-off mapping sessions with solutions engineers
Run policy-diff test harness that evaluates known edge-case scenarios (delegated roles, resource-scoped bindings)
Scale audit-forwarding buffers and add auto-throttle alerts to avoid drops
Use checksums + sequence numbers per object and a reconciliation Lambda to auto-heal small divergences
Automate cutover steps as much as possible and require two-person approval for final wave
notes: We plan a tabletop exercise with oncall, security, solutions engineering, and PMs on 2026-03-21 to rehearse wave failure scenarios. Bring the rollback toggle runbook and incident severities matrix.
